title: Those who dwelt in Jerusalem: priests “a thousand and seven hundred and threescore” — or 822, 242 and 128?
summary: 1 Chronicles 9 and Nehemiah 11 list the same houses of Jerusalem’s inhabitants, many of the same names. The totals differ: Benjamin 956 or 928, the priests’ brethren 1,760 or 1,192 (822 + 242 + 128), the porters 212 or 172.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 9:9: “And their brethren, according to their generations, nine hundred and fifty and six. All these men were chief of the fathers in the house of their fathers.” Hebrew (WLC) 9:9: וַאֲחֵיהֶם֙ לְתֹ֣לְדֹותָ֔ם תְּשַׁ֥ע מֵאֹ֖ות וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֑ה כָּל־אֵ֣לֶּה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים רָאשֵׁ֥י אָבֹ֖ות לְבֵ֥ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃    ס KJV 1 Chronicles 9:13: “And their brethren, heads of the house of their fathers, a thousand and seven hundred and threescore; very able men for the work of the service of the house of God.” Hebrew (WLC) 9:13: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֗ם רָאשִׁים֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹותָ֔ם אֶ֕לֶף וּשְׁבַ֥ע מֵאֹ֖ות וְשִׁשִּׁ֑ים גִּבֹּ֣ורֵי חֵ֔יל מְלֶ֖אכֶת עֲבֹודַ֥ת בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 9:22: “All these which were chosen to be porters in the gates were two hundred and twelve. These were reckoned by their genealogy in their villages, whom David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their set office.” Hebrew (WLC) 9:22: כֻּלָּ֤ם הַבְּרוּרִים֙ לְשֹׁעֲרִ֣ים בַּסִּפִּ֔ים מָאתַ֖יִם וּשְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֑ר הֵ֤מָּה בְחַצְרֵיהֶם֙ הִתְיַחְשָׂ֔ם הֵ֣מָּה יִסַּ֥ד דָּוִ֛יד וּשְׁמוּאֵ֥ל הָרֹאֶ֖ה בֶּאֱמוּנָתָֽם׃ KJV Nehemiah 11:8: “And after him Gabbai, Sallai, nine hundred twenty and eight.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:8: וְאַחֲרָ֖יו גַּבַּ֣י סַלָּ֑י תְּשַׁ֥ע מֵאֹ֖ות עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנָֽה׃ KJV Nehemiah 11:12: “And their brethren that did the work of the house were eight hundred twenty and two: and Adaiah the son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashur, the son of Malchiah.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:12: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֗ם עֹשֵׂ֤י הַמְּלָאכָה֙ לַבַּ֔יִת שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵאֹ֖ות עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וּשְׁנָ֑יִם וַ֠עֲדָיָה בֶּן־יְרֹחָ֤ם בֶּן־פְּלַלְיָה֙ בֶּן־אַמְצִ֣י בֶן־זְכַרְיָ֔ה בֶּן־פַּשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן־מַלְכִּיָּֽה׃ KJV Nehemiah 11:13: “And his brethren, chief of the fathers, two hundred forty and two: and Amashai the son of Azareel, the son of Ahasai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,” Hebrew (WLC) 11:13: וְאֶחָיו֙ רָאשִׁ֣ים לְאָבֹ֔ות מָאתַ֖יִם אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וּשְׁנָ֑יִם וַעֲמַשְׁסַ֧י בֶּן־עֲזַרְאֵ֛ל בֶּן־אַחְזַ֥י בֶּן־מְשִׁלֵּמֹ֖ות בֶּן־אִמֵּֽר׃ KJV Nehemiah 11:14: “And their brethren, mighty men of valour, an hundred twenty and eight: and their overseer was Zabdiel, the son of one of the great men.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:14: וַאֲחֵיהֶם֙ גִּבֹּ֣ורֵי חַ֔יִל מֵאָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וּשְׁמֹנָ֑ה וּפָקִ֣יד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם זַבְדִּיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־הַגְּדֹולִֽים׃    ס KJV Nehemiah 11:19: “Moreover the porters, Akkub, Talmon, and their brethren that kept the gates, were an hundred seventy and two.” Hebrew (WLC) 11:19: וְהַשֹּֽׁועֲרִים֙ עַקּ֣וּב טַלְמֹ֔ון וַאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַשֹּׁמְרִ֣ים בַּשְּׁעָרִ֑ים מֵאָ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם׃ Septuagint (Brenton) 1 Chronicles 9:9, 9:13 and 9:22 print 956, 1,760 and 212, as the Hebrew does. reasoning: The two chapters name largely the same houses in the same order: Jedaiah and Jachin; a son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub (Azariah in Chronicles, Seraiah in Nehemiah); Adaiah son of Jeroham son of Pashur son of Malchijah; a descendant of Immer (Maasiai or Amashai); Shemaiah son of Hashub; Mattaniah son of Micah son of Asaph; Akkub and Talmon. Some names are spelled differently and some ancestors are named in one list only. The totals do not match. Benjamin: 956 against 928. The priests: 1 Chronicles 9:13 gives one sum, 1,760, for “their brethren, heads of the house of their fathers”; Nehemiah 11:12-14 gives three, 822 + 242 + 128 = 1,192, a difference of 568. The porters: 212 against 172. The KJV, the Hebrew and the Greek of 1 Chronicles agree with each other in each place.
scope: Untagged. The two chapters may describe different dates or different ways of counting: 1 Chronicles 9:1-2 speaks of “the first inhabitants” and Nehemiah 11:1-3 of those who dwelt in Jerusalem after the lots were cast, and the one list says “heads of the house of their fathers” where the other says “that did the work of the house”. Neither text says the two counts are of the same moment, so the record states a difference in figures and does not say which is right or that one copies the other. Nehemiah 11 was read in the Hebrew and the KJV only; Brenton’s Greek of Nehemiah was not fetched. No word was argued from its Hebrew root. title: Who dwelt in Jerusalem: Judah, Benjamin, “Ephraim, and Manasseh” — or Judah and Benjamin only?
summary: 1 Chronicles 9:3 lists four tribes among the dwellers of Jerusalem. The parallel verse, Nehemiah 11:4, lists two.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 9:3: “And in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasseh;” Hebrew (WLC) 9:3: וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ יָשְׁב֔וּ מִן־בְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּמִן־בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן וּמִן־בְּנֵ֥י אֶפְרַ֖יִם וּמְנַשֶּֽׁה׃ KJV Nehemiah 11:4: “And at Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin. reasoning: The opening of Nehemiah 11:4 reads as 1 Chronicles 9:3 does, with the same verb and first two tribes. 1 Chronicles 9:3 goes on to add Ephraim and Manasseh; Nehemiah 11:4 stops at Benjamin and turns to the sons of Judah. title: David’s count of the Levites: “from the age of thirty years” — or “from twenty years old”?
summary: 1 Chronicles 23:3 numbers the Levites from thirty years old and gives 38,000. Twenty-four verses on, the same chapter says the Levites were numbered from twenty, “by the last words of David”.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 23:3: “Now the Levites were numbered from the age of thirty years and upward: and their number by their polls, man by man, was thirty and eight thousand.” Hebrew (WLC) 23:3: וַיִּסָּֽפְרוּ֙ הַלְוִיִּ֔ם מִבֶּ֛ן שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה וַיְהִ֨י מִסְפָּרָ֤ם לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָם֙ לִגְבָרִ֔ים שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁמֹונָ֖ה אָֽלֶף׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 23:24: “These were the sons of Levi after the house of their fathers; even the chief of the fathers, as they were counted by number of names by their polls, that did the work for the service of the house of the Lord, from the age of twenty years and upward.” Hebrew (WLC) 23:24: אֵ֣לֶּה בְנֵֽי־לֵוִי֩ לְבֵ֨ית אֲבֹתֵיהֶ֜ם רָאשֵׁ֧י הָאָבֹ֣ות לִפְקוּדֵיהֶ֗ם בְּמִסְפַּ֤ר שֵׁמֹות֙ לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָ֔ם עֹשֵׂה֙ הַמְּלָאכָ֔ה לַעֲבֹדַ֖ת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וָמָֽעְלָה׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 23:27: “For by the last words of David the Levites were numbered from twenty years old and above:” Hebrew (WLC) 23:27: כִּ֣י בְדִבְרֵ֤י דָוִיד֙ הָאַ֣חֲרֹנִ֔ים הֵ֖מָּה מִסְפַּ֣ר בְּנֵי־לֵוִ֑י מִבֶּ֛ן עֶשְׂרִ֥ים שָׁנָ֖ה וּלְמָֽעְלָה׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 23:3: Καὶ ἠρίθμησαν οἱ Λευῖται ἀπὸ τριακονταετοῦς καὶ ἐπάνω, καὶ ἐγένετο ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτῶν κατὰ κεφαλὴν αὐτῶν εἰς ἄνδρας τριάκοντα καὶ ὀκτὼ χιλιάδας. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 23:27: Ὅτι ἐν τοῖς λόγοις Δαυὶδ τοῖς ἐσχάτοις ἐστὶν ὁ ἀριθμὸς υἱῶν Λευὶ ἀπὸ εἰκοσαετοῦς καὶ ἐπάνω· Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH23.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/23/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH23.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1CH23.htm.

Verse 3 gives thirty and a total of 38,000, split in verses 4-5 into 24,000, 6,000, 4,000 and 4,000 (which does add to 38,000). Verses 24 and 27 give twenty, and verse 27 says that is by David’s last words. title: “Spake I a word to any of the judges of Israel” — the Greek has “tribe”, as 2 Samuel 7:7 does
summary: The KJV of 1 Chronicles 17:6 has God ask whether he spoke to any of the “judges” of Israel. Brenton’s Greek has “one tribe”. The Hebrew of 2 Samuel 7:7, the parallel verse, has a different noun from 1 Chronicles 17:6: שִׁבְטֵי, “tribes” in the KJV.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 17:6: “Wheresoever I have walked with all Israel, spake I a word to any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why have ye not built me an house of cedars?” Hebrew (WLC) 17:6: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שֹׁפְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֛יתִי לִרְעֹ֥ות אֶת־עַמִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 17:6: καὶ ἤμην ἐν σκηνῇ καὶ ἐν καλὺμματι ἐν πᾶσιν οἷς διῆλθον ἐν παντὶ Ἰσραήλ· εἰ λαλῶν ἐλάλησα πρὸς μίαν φυλὴν τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ οἷς ἐνετειλάμην τοῦ ποιμαίνειν τὸν λαόν μου, λέγων, ὅτι οὐκ ᾠκοδομήσατέ μοι οἶκον κέδρινον; Brenton English: “in all places through which I have gone with all Israel: did I ever speak to any one tribe of Israel whom I commanded to feed my people, saying, Why is it that ye have not built me a house of cedar?” KJV 2 Samuel 7:7: “In all the places wherein I have walked with all the children of Israel spake I a word with any of the tribes of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people Israel, saying, Why build ye not me an house of cedar?” Hebrew (WLC) 7:7: בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶֽׁר־הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי֮ בְּכָל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ הֲדָבָ֣ר דִּבַּ֗רְתִּי אֶת־אַחַד֙ שִׁבְטֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּ֗יתִי לִרְעֹ֛ות אֶת־עַמִּ֥י אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לָ֛מָּה לֹֽא־בְנִיתֶ֥ם לִ֖י בֵּ֥ית אֲרָזִֽים׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 7:7: ἐν πᾶσιν οἷς διῆλθον ἐν παντὶ Ἰσραήλ· εἰ λαλῶν ἐλάλησα πρὸς μίαν φυλὴν τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ, ᾧ ἐνετειλάμην ποιμαίνειν τὸν λαόν μου Ἰσραὴλ, λέγων, ἱνατί οὐκ ᾠκοδομήκατέ μοι οἶκον κέδρινον; Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2SA07.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/17/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/10/7/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1CH17.htm and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2SA07.htm.
reasoning: The KJV of 1 Chronicles 17:6 says “judges”, and the Hebrew prints שֹׁפְטֵי (a plural noun of the root the KJV renders “judge”). Brenton’s Greek of the same verse says “one tribe” (μίαν φυλήν), the reading of the Hebrew in 2 Samuel 7:7 and of Brenton’s Greek there. A plainly different noun, “judges” or “tribes”, stands in the same slot of the parallel speech.

title: “I will settle him in mine house and in my kingdom” — the Greek has “his kingdom”, and 2 Samuel 7:16 has “thine house and thy kingdom”
summary: In the KJV God settles David’s son “in mine house and in my kingdom”. The Hebrew says “my kingdom”; Brenton’s Greek says “his kingdom”. In the parallel promise, 2 Samuel 7:16, the house and kingdom are David’s: “thine house and thy kingdom”.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 17:14: “But I will settle him in mine house and in my kingdom for ever: and his throne shall be established for evermore.” Hebrew (WLC) 17:14: וְהַֽעֲמַדְתִּ֛יהוּ בְּבֵיתִ֥י וּבְמַלְכוּתִ֖י עַד־הָעֹולָ֑ם וְכִסְאֹ֕ו יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכֹ֖ון עַד־עֹולָֽם׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 17:14: Καὶ πιστώσω αὐτὸν ἐν οἴκῳ μου καὶ ἐν βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ ἕως αἰῶνος, καὶ ὁ θρόνος αὐτοῦ ἔσται ἀνωρθωμένος ἕως αἰῶνος. Brenton English: “And I will establish him in my house and in his kingdom for ever; and his throne shall be set up for ever.” KJV 2 Samuel 7:16: “And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.” Hebrew (WLC) 7:16: וְנֶאְמַ֨ן בֵּיתְךָ֧ וּמַֽמְלַכְתְּךָ֛ עַד־עֹולָ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כִּֽסְאֲךָ֔ יִהְיֶ֥ה נָכֹ֖ון עַד־עֹולָֽם׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 7:16: Καὶ πιστωθήσεται ὁ οἶκος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἡ βασιλεία αὐτοῦ ἕως αἰῶνος ἐνώπιόν μου· καὶ ὁ θρόνος αὐτοῦ ἔσται ἀνωρθωμένος εἰς τον αἰῶνα. Brenton English: “And his house shall be made sure, and his kingdom for ever before me, and his throne shall be set up for ever.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2SA07.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/17/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/10/7/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/1CH17.htm, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2SA07.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2SA07.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew of 1 Chronicles 17:14 prints בְּבֵיתִי וּבְמַלְכוּתִי, “in my house, in my kingdom”, with a first-person ending on both nouns. The Hebrew of 2 Samuel 7:16 prints בֵּיתְךָ וּמַמְלַכְתְּךָ, “your house, your kingdom”, with a second-person ending. Brenton’s Greek of 1 Chronicles 17:14 changes the second to “his kingdom” (αὐτοῦ), a third reading. The three texts name three different owners of the kingdom in the parallel promise.
scope: T applies at 1 Chronicles 17:14, Septuagint only (the second noun). The Hebrew ‘my house, my kingdom’ is rendered correctly by the KJV. The Hebrew difference from 2 Samuel 7:16 is a difference between two books and is reported as such; it is not a Hebrew mistranslation. title: Fetching the ark: the whole congregation “from Shihor of Egypt even unto the entering of Hemath” — or “the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand”?
summary: In 1 Chronicles 13 David takes counsel with the captains and gathers all Israel from Egypt to Hemath. In 2 Samuel 6:1 he gathers “the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand”.
text: KJV 1 Chronicles 13:1: “And David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds, and with every leader.” Hebrew (WLC) 13:1: וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ דָּוִ֗יד עִם־שָׂרֵ֧י הָאֲלָפִ֛ים וְהַמֵּאֹ֖ות לְכָל־נָגִֽיד׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 13:5: “So David gathered all Israel together, from Shihor of Egypt even unto the entering of Hemath, to bring the ark of God from Kirjathjearim.” Hebrew (WLC) 13:5: וַיַּקְהֵ֤ל דָּוִיד֙ אֶת־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִן־שִׁיחֹ֥ור מִצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־לְבֹ֣וא חֲמָ֑ת לְהָבִיא֙ אֶת־אֲרֹ֣ון הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מִקִּרְיַ֖ת יְעָרִֽים׃ KJV 2 Samuel 6:1: “Again, David gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.” Hebrew (WLC) 6:1: וַיֹּ֨סֶף עֹ֥וד דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־כָּל־בָּח֥וּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃ Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 6:1: Καὶ συνήγαγεν ἔτι Δαυὶδ πάντα νεανίαν ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ, ὡς ἑβδομήκοντα χιλιάδας. reasoning: Both books tell the first attempt to bring the ark from the house of Abinadab. Chronicles names the gathered body “all Israel”, from the Egyptian border to the entry of Hemath, after a council with the captains of thousands and hundreds; the body is not given a number. title: The sons of Simeon: six names in Genesis, five in Numbers and 1 Chronicles — and not the same five
summary: Genesis 46:10 names six sons of Simeon. Numbers 26:12 and 1 Chronicles 4:24 each name five, and they differ from each other and from Genesis.
text: KJV Genesis 46:10: “And the sons of Simeon; Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad, and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul the son of a Canaanitish woman.” Hebrew (WLC) 46:10: וּבְנֵ֣י שִׁמְעֹ֗ון יְמוּאֵ֧ל וְיָמִ֛ין וְאֹ֖הַד וְיָכִ֣ין וְצֹ֑חַר וְשָׁא֖וּל בֶּן־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִֽית׃ KJV Numbers 26:12: “The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites: of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites: of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites:” Hebrew (WLC) 26:12: בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְעֹון֮ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם֒ לִנְמוּאֵ֗ל מִשְׁפַּ֙חַת֙ הַנְּמ֣וּאֵלִ֔י לְיָמִ֕ין מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיָּמִינִ֑י לְיָכִ֕ין מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַיָּכִינִֽי׃ KJV 1 Chronicles 4:24: “The sons of Simeon were, Nemuel, and Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul:” Hebrew (WLC) 4:24: בְּנֵ֖י שִׁמְעֹ֑ון נְמוּאֵ֣ל וְיָמִ֔ין יָרִ֖יב זֶ֥רַח שָׁאֽוּל׃ Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/GEN46.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/NUM26.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1CH04.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/1/46/, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/4/26/ and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/13/4/.
reasoning: Genesis 46:10: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, Shaul (six). Numbers 26:12 (clans): Nemuel, Jamin, Jachin, Zerah, Shaul (five; Ohad is absent and Zohar is Zerah). 1 Chronicles 4:24: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul (five; Ohad is absent, and Jarib stands where Numbers has Jachin). The list in Chronicles agrees with the Numbers list in four names out of five, and with Genesis in two.
scope: Untagged. Names that differ by a letter or two (Jemuel and Nemuel, Zohar and Zerah, Jarib and Jachin) may be variant spellings or second names of one son; the texts do not say so. Ohad appears only in Genesis 46:10, which may be because he had no clan (Numbers lists clans). The record compares the printed names and counts; it does not say any text is wrong and does not argue from silence about Ohad’s descendants. No Greek text was fetched. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
